clue.text: 14 down's financial advice given years after one in rest-home perished

indicators.note: the years abbreviation is placed after the rearranged letters
something perished has fallen apart, so the letters of these words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim tale of someone who died in a care home, followed by advice about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perished' shuffles ONEINRESTHOME into THEREISNOMONE, and 'after' puts Y at the end. The definition refers to the note Liam Byrne (14 down) left for his Treasury successor in 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: Byrne's notorious handover note to his successor said simply that the coffers were empty, a piece of fiscal counsel.

clue.text: Square it with American emperor

parts.note: a T-square, so T can stand for square
taken as written
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A plea to make peace with an American ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor of the first century AD, an example of the class.

clue.text: Neo in time left old Penny for Beryl

indicators.note: the setter's pronoun goes inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Neo is the setter, so the setter refers to himself as ME
D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: The setter musing on a past when an old penny was left behind for someone called Beryl.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves to clue ME. 'Beryl' looks like a woman's name but is the mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: The green gemstone is a variety of the mineral beryl, so the specific stone stands for its parent mineral.

clue.text: European Cup, Italy's ground, and some trees

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the country's name, its possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A football report: the European Cup played at an Italian ground, with some trees nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as a stadium but is the anagram signal, turning CUPITALY into UCALYPTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum trees of the Australian genus, given here in their Latin plural, form a group of trees.

clue.text: Charming Prince Otto gorged on a root vegetable

parts.note: charming means sweet, delightful

indicators.note: the name has swallowed the letter, so it sits inside

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale Prince Charming named Otto stuffing himself with a root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming Prince' reads as the fairy-tale hero, but splits into SWEET and P.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-fleshed tuber of a tropical vine is eaten as a root vegetable.

clue.text: Eggs tossed around in Benfica v Osasuna

indicators.note: tossed around suggests a turn, so the letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Eggs thrown during a football match between Benfica and Osasuna.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds AVO within 'Benfica v Osasuna', and 'tossed around' turns it back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural for egg cells, used in biology for female reproductive cells.

clue.text: Franco-German affirmations for board

parts.note: the French word for yes
the German word for yes

explanation.surface: French and German leaders agreeing with one another at a board meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is said to combine the French and German words for yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lettered board used in seances to spell out supposed messages from spirits.

clue.text: Maybe G8 leaders to end talks after month

indicators.note: the leading letters come after the month

parts.note: OCT is the short form of October

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Heads of the Group of Eight nations aiming to finish their summit within a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the definition as an example: the G8 had eight members.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight, such as the G8 nations, is a set of eight, the musical term for an eightsome.

clue.text: National PM twice denied Democrat

indicators.note: denied means refused, so the letter for Democrat is taken away

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was British Prime Minister twice, in 1868 and 1874-80

explanation.surface: A prime minister twice refused a Democrat's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective but is a noun: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a Middle Eastern country is one of its nationals.

clue.text: Moving about meant carrying correct change

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the rearranged word holds the other piece
moving about means shuffling, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to mend is to correct or put right

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a correction about while moving it around a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving about' shuffles MEANT into AMENT, which 'carrying' wraps around MEND.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration to a text or law, such as a constitutional revision.

clue.text: Electra stirred the syrup

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Electra, the Greek tragic heroine, stirring syrup in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirred' rearranges ELECTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark molasses-like syrup produced in sugar refining, a British kitchen staple.

clue.text: Goddess found in A&E

indicators.note: in says the word for found goes inside the two letters

parts.note: A and E taken as written
to found is to start or establish

explanation.surface: A goddess discovered in a hospital accident and emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like 'discovered' but is the verb meaning establish, giving START between A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A Phoenician deity of fertility and war, an ancient Middle Eastern goddess.

clue.text: Place for single animal — that's hedge

definitions.meaning: a compartment in a stable or byre for one horse or cow
to hedge is to play for time or be evasive

explanation.surface: A farmer explaining a pen for one animal, bordered by a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means a single animal's compartment in a barn and also the verb to delay or prevaricate.

clue.text: Drunken boss one in scrum

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
the head is the boss

explanation.surface: A drunk boss getting stuck into a rugby scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrum is the set-piece in rugby where the forwards bind and push.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby prop forward on the right of the front row, one player in the scrum.

clue.text: Retiring chap has drunken drongo on toast

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so this comes first
drunken suggests staggering, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to toast bread is to brown it

explanation.surface: A shy man with a drunken idiot sprawled on toast; drongo is Australian slang for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like 'shy' but refers to the former Prime Minister who was leaving politics at the time. 'drunken' rearranges DRONGO into GORDON.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Labour Prime Minister was stepping down as an MP when this puzzle appeared, a retiring man.

clue.text: Good riddance to contented, stable employee

indicators.note: riddance means getting rid of, so the letter for good is removed

parts.note: glad means pleased or contented

explanation.surface: An employee in a steady job saying good riddance to contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' reads as steady, but means a horse stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable boy who looks after racehorses is known in Britain as a stable hand of this kind.

clue.text: Post returned by British sailors, ashore at last for realistic treasury man

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: post means mail
taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's sailors

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Mail sent back by British sailors who have come ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns MAIL round. He was Chief Secretary to the Treasury in 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour politician was Chief Secretary to the Treasury in 2010 and left a frank note admitting the coffers were bare.

clue.text: Rev is playing on piano, having introduced giants' musical style

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the piano letter

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the giants into their middle
playing suggests sporting about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: ogres are giants in folklore

explanation.surface: A clergyman playing piano, including some music about giants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' shuffles REVIS into RSIVE, which takes in OGRES after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Prog rock, an experimental rock genre of the 1970s, is a musical style.

clue.text: Worker in dock — first wife died in shop

indicators.note: in places the wife and died abbreviation inside the shop

parts.note: a store is a shop
Eve was the first wife, in Genesis

explanation.surface: A worker on trial in the dock because his first wife died in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' suggests a courtroom but means a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A docker who loads and unloads ships is a labourer at a port.

clue.text: Reasonable to fill pipe again broken as uninspected purchase

indicators.note: the two letters go inside to fill the rearranged words
broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OK means acceptable or reasonable

explanation.surface: Someone's pipe broken again and refilled, bought without checking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges PIPEAGAIN into APIGINAPE, and OK goes in before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something bought sight unseen, from the old trick of selling a cat in a sack as a piglet.

clue.text: See writer is Swift, having name for Lilliput's leader

indicators.note: having one letter for another means swapping them

parts.note: the writer is the setter, so this gives I'M
swift means agile

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A literary note: the writer is Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, who named Lilliput.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like the author but means agile. N replaces the L of I'M AGILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something in the mind is to visualise it, as in see it in one's head.

clue.text: Aeroplane prank gets son ejected

indicators.note: ejected means thrown out, so the son letter goes

parts.note: a jest is a joke or prank

explanation.surface: A boy thrown out of an aircraft after a practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejected' suits the plane picture but takes S from JEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane powered by a jet engine is commonly called by that engine type.

clue.text: Having diamonds only shows integrity

parts.note: just means only, merely
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Owning only diamonds reveals someone's honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness and moral rightness, the quality of being upright.

clue.text: Bill enters revamped BBC home to forage

indicators.note: enters says the account goes inside the rearranged letters
revamped means made over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's bill arriving at the revamped BBC headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revamped' shuffles BBCHOME into BEHCOMB, and AC goes after BE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour the shore for objects washed up is a form of searching or scavenging.

clue.text: Husband's somewhat loose garment

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband; the 's means 'is'
a bit means somewhat

explanation.surface: A husband's clothing is a bit baggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' looks like it qualifies 'loose', but gives A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's or nun's robe is a long loose garment.

clue.text: Amenhotep, so mighty, captures Derby town

indicators.note: captures means holds within, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: The Egyptian pharaoh Amenhotep, so powerful he seized a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous horse race run at this Surrey town, not the city of Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey town hosts the famous Derby horse race on its downs, so it is the race's town.

clue.text: See 1 across
God in London district creates atmospheric effect

parts.note: Ra was the Egyptian sun god
taken as written
Bow is a district in east London

explanation.surface: A deity in a London neighbourhood producing a weather effect.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an area of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlight refracted through raindrops forms a coloured arc, an optical phenomenon of the sky.

clue.text: Montgomery the jazzer in stitch- up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads backwards, from the bottom

parts.note: to sew is to stitch

explanation.surface: A jazz guitarist caught up in a frame-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stitch-up' reads as a frame, but splits: stitch is SEW, and 'up' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wes Montgomery was an influential American jazz guitarist.

clue.text: University type, in love with Scotsman, stays overnight in Rome?

indicators.note: in says the Roman night sits inside the love and Scotsman letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so O
Ian is a typical Scottish name
night in Latin is NOX; over says it is read backwards, giving XON

explanation.surface: A student in love with a Scotsman, staying the night in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overnight' splits into 'over' (reverse) and 'night', which 'in Rome' puts into Latin, NOX.
explanation.definitionFit: A member or graduate of Oxford University is described as an Oxford person by this name.

clue.text: Still time to ride competitively

parts.note: even means still, as in 'even more' and 'still more'

explanation.surface: There is still time to race on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'there is yet', but gives EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the equestrian discipline of dressage, cross-country and jumping, so to compete in it is to take part on horseback.

clue.text: Truly evil bank entertains heartless crime

indicators.note: entertains means holds as a guest, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: sin means evil or wrongdoing
to bank on is to rely on

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A wicked bank hosting a crime with its heart cut out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves C and E, which go between SIN and RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter sign-off meaning genuinely or honestly.
